Synopsis:
The dialog with the djinni who was trapped in the lamp.Touching the lamp means he's freed, but the person who touched it is now INSIDE the lamp. This dialogue occurs with one of the players outside of the lamp.Yafeu is hovering above the lamp, this player is right in front of the lamp.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_DjinniTrap_Antagonist.json: Yafeu is a djinni who was trapped in a lamp and has just been released — but the lamp’s curse swapped places: whoever touched the lamp is now trapped inside it. The current player stands just outside the lamp while their companion (or the person they freed) remains confined inside and out of view. Yafeu is hovering above the lamp, speaking in a mocking, antagonistic tone and was already addressing other onlookers when the swap occurred, so he taunts and misreads the freed player’s relationship to the captive (calling them “master,” “servant,” or even assuming prostitution). Nearby companions or NPCs witnessed the djinni’s speech, so the player’s lines respond both to recent imprisonment/swap and to Yafeu’s provocations.
- LOW_DjinniTrap_Antagonist_Interrupted.json: The player has just freed themselves after being trapped inside a lamp; this interrupts Yafeu, a djinni who was speaking with the rest of the party. Yafeu reacts with shock, but his tone can range from mocking and unstable to sarcastically helpful, and some responses imply grudging servitude. Depending on the player's reply the scene can immediately escalate — Yafeu may goad the player, suggest destroying the lamp, or prepare for combat. The other party members are present off‑screen and witnessing the exchange.

context: Yafeu is a djinni who has just burst free of a cursed lamp, but the lamp’s magic swapped places: the person who touched it is now trapped inside and out of sight. The current player stands directly outside the lamp while their companion (or the person they freed) is confined within. Yafeu hovers above the lamp in a mocking, antagonistic mood, taunting the player and deliberately misreading the captive relationship (calling them “master,” “servant,” or implying prostitution).
